features.description: Issue #282 redesign applies a responsive light/dark system, refreshed portfolio sections, contact paths, and accessible navigation.
steps: Open home in light and dark themes
Verify responsive hero, projects, about, contact, and footer
Verify preference persistence and keyboard navigation
evidence: Implemented issue #282 visual specification with self-hosted Clash Display, semantic tokens, persistent theme control, refreshed sections, and contact links.
Contact section card uses the shared centered 1240px section container and responsive horizontal padding.
Theme toggle transparent background, border, icon color, 18px moon/sun SVGs, and hover state match apps.oprimo.dev.
Footer link hover color matches the desktop navigation link hover color.
Footer displays the JG brand mark and keeps José Guilherme in the dynamic copyright line, matching Stitch.
Outlined hero and GitHub project buttons have a brighter hover surface and border in dark mode; light-mode hover colors are unchanged.
Mobile menu link hover uses the surface-active token in light and dark themes.
Project technology chips use compact padding and gaps below 375px, keeping six-tag cards within two rows at 320px.
Technology chips remain content-height when the reserved tag slot has extra vertical space.
All links and buttons use a pointer cursor through the global stylesheet.
Production browser checked both themes, mobile menu Escape/focus restoration, project images, and 320, 390, 768, 1024, and 1440px widths.
About uses an unboxed editorial layout at every size; the divider is vertical on desktop and horizontal between stacked sections on mobile and tablet.
About content uses the same bordered, rounded semantic card surface as Contact.
All JSX links use Next.js Link, preserving existing hrefs, attributes, and styling.
Browser review at 320px, 390px, 768px, 1023px, 1024px, and 1440px confirmed stacked mobile/tablet layout, two-column desktop layout, and no horizontal overflow.
Light and dark desktop layouts both use the unboxed editorial columns and theme-specific header-divider token.
The browser favicon uses the header's JG wordmark without a tile and adapts its text color to the system theme.
/icon.svg returned 200, parsed as valid XML, and was included in the production build.
npm run lint, npx tsc --noEmit, and npm run build passed after the desktop About layout change.
